newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market quiet,no bids-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market quiet,no bids-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Thursday were quiet, with no reported bids or sales, feedlot sources said.

Bids were expected to surface at $62.00 to $63.00 per cwt, with owners asking $64.00 for cattle not sold, they said. Many feedlots reportedly were current following this week's sales at $63.00, the sources said.
Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots were close to sold out of market-ready cattle and several Kansas cattle feeders said sales were strong, but some lots had cattle left to sell.
Demand for cattle was slowing amid lower beef prices, with packers said to have adequate supplies of live inventory for the near term, feedlot sources said.
Packers also were taking as long as possible to pick up cattle that were sold last week, with some asking for 10 to 12 days to pick up cattle instead of the usual seven, they said.
The large buildup of cattle inventories could result in lighter slaughter schedules, especially if beef demand softens, sources said.
